metadata.name: Ecodesign for Kotlin
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Kotlin code, on Android as much as on the server: scoped coroutines, no blocking on a thread, bounded channels and collections.

coroutines.name: Kotlin — coroutines and threads
coroutines.description: Give every coroutine a lifetime, never block a thread waiting (RGESN Algorithms, GR491_Backend_4).

rules.title: GlobalScope coroutine
rules.description: A coroutine launched in GlobalScope outlives the screen, the request or the component that started it. On a phone that means work and radio use continuing for a screen the user has already left.
rules.recommendation: Launch from a scope with a lifetime: viewModelScope, lifecycleScope, or a CoroutineScope you cancel yourself. Cancellation then propagates to the children.

rules.title: Blocking call inside a coroutine
rules.description: runBlocking, or Thread.sleep inside a suspending function, pins a thread that the dispatcher could have given to other work. A handful of them is enough to starve a pool and keep cores busy waiting.
rules.recommendation: Use delay() in suspending code, and move genuinely blocking work to Dispatchers.IO with withContext. Keep runBlocking for main() and tests.

rules.title: Unbounded channel
rules.description: Channel(UNLIMITED) removes the back-pressure that would have told the producer to slow down. The queue then grows to whatever memory allows, and the work is done twice: once to enqueue, once to discard.
rules.recommendation: Size the channel to what the consumer can absorb, and choose the overflow behaviour deliberately (SUSPEND, DROP_OLDEST).

collections.name: Kotlin — collections and allocations
collections.description: Do not materialise a collection you only walk once (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Intermediate collection in a chain
rules.description: Each map or filter on a List allocates a new List. Chained three deep over a large collection, that is three full copies for one result that a sequence would have produced without any of them.
rules.recommendation: Switch the chain to asSequence() when the collection is large, and materialise only the final result. On small collections the plain list stays clearer and cheaper.
rules.note: A single asSequence() anywhere in the file silences the rule, even for other chains that still materialise. On a small collection the plain list is both clearer and cheaper, so a hit is a question about volume, not a defect.

rules.title: Linear search inside a loop
rules.description: contains on a List walks it from the start. Called for every element of another collection, the work becomes quadratic and collapses on volumes that were fine in testing.
rules.recommendation: Index into a Set or a Map before the loop, and look up in constant time.
rules.note: Declaring one Set or Map in the file silences the rule. contains on a short list is perfectly fine; what matters is whether this particular lookup sits inside a loop over a large collection.
